text: Ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ἀνδρέαν ἀπολογίᾳ. Non videtur exstare hæc Apologia. Ejus meminit Cyrillus in Commonitorio ad Eulogium, et conjungit, cum Apologia seu responsione ad Theodoretum : Καὶ ἀντιρρήσεις παρ' ἐμοῦ γεγραμμένας πρὸς τοὺς γράψαντας κατὰ τῶν Κεφαλαίων· δύο δέ εἰσιν ἐπίσκοποι Ἀνδρέας καὶ Θεοδώρητος. Refutationes quas contra Andream et Theodoretum episcopos, qui adversus Capita scripserunt, edidi.
anchorLine: τον τῶν κεφαλαίων ἀπολογία (r), οὕτω λέγων·
en: In the Apology to Andreas. This Apology does not appear to survive. Cyril mentions it in his Commonitorium to Eulogius and joins it with the response to Theodoret: 'and the refutations written by me against those who wrote against the Chapters; the two are bishops, Andreas and Theodoret.' [Latin gloss:] The refutations which I published against Andreas and Theodoret, bishops, who wrote against the Chapters.

en: The printed editions of Gregory read τῆς φύσεως (of nature).

text: Marg. Fr. Ἡ σύνταξις· Μηδετέρας τῶν φωνῶν, τοῦ δύο, καὶ ἕν, ἀναιρουμένων· ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀεὶ μὲν κειμένων καὶ λεγομένων εὐσεβῶς. Syntaxis hæc est : Neutra vocum, duarum aut unius, alteram perimente ; sed quæ in eodem Christo semper ponantur, et pie de eo dicantur.
unreadable: Note text clear (under heading VARIÆ LECTIONES). The raised call 83 could not be found in the Greek column: the likely lines (μηδ' ἑτέρας τῶν φωνῶν, τούτων / ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀεὶ μὲν κειμένων…) show no visible raised numeral at 600 dpi.
en: Marginal reading of Fr.: The construction is: with neither of the terms, 'two' or 'one', removing the other; but with things that are always posited in the same Christ and spoken of piously. [Latin gloss:] The construction is this: neither of the words, 'two' or 'one', is to destroy the other; but they are to be laid down of the same Christ and spoken of him piously.

text: Τὴν διαίρεσιν τροπώσασθαι. Exponit [damaged, ...]ych. τὸ τροποῦσθαι, ἁρμόζεσθαι, nec aliter hic loci exponi possit, si negat, retineamus ; quia sublata, esset potius eliminare, exterere ac abdicare divisionem, quod nisi vocibus significantibus unitionem positis, recte ait Maximus non posse intelligi.
anchorLine: ρεσιν τροπώσασθαι (s) οὐ γινώσκομεν· ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τοῦ
unreadable: The authority named after Exponit is ink-damaged: only '...ych.' survives (probably Hesych. but not read, not completed). The phrase 'si negat, retineamus' is as printed; sense uncertain.
en: 'To turn (the division) aside.' [Authority damaged, ...ych.] explains τροποῦσθαι as ἁρμόζεσθαι (to be adjusted), and the phrase cannot be explained otherwise in this place; as for the clause as printed, once it is removed it would rather mean to eliminate, expel and abdicate division, which, unless words signifying union are laid down, Maximus rightly says cannot be understood.

en: Maximus appears to have recognised the end of the letter here; the following seems to be sewn on from elsewhere.

text: Ἀδιαιρέτως. Reg. cod. et Venet. ἀδιαιρέτους, quod respiceret τὰς φύσεις. Alias enim, et referendo ad subsistentes, falsa esset propositio et Nestoriana : quodque proclive masculina in Christo absolute prolata personæ videantur, melius alii ἀδιαιρέτως, quæ est ipsa Cyrilli vox, quam Maximus exponit.
anchorLine: παρ' ἑαυτῷ μὲν, τὸ δύο λέγειν ἀδιαιρέτως (t), ὀρ-
unreadable: Marker glyph prints close to (l)/(t); read t because the letters run s, t.
en: Reg. manuscript and Venet. have ἀδιαιρέτους (indivisible, plural), which would refer to the natures (τὰς φύσεις). Otherwise, referring to the subsistents, the proposition would be false and Nestorian; and because masculine forms said absolutely of Christ readily seem to refer to the person, others read ἀδιαιρέτως (indivisibly), which is Cyril's own word, and which Maximus explains.

en: These words do not occur in Cyril's Scholia as they survive. Both letters to Succensus press similar points throughout. See Damascene, book III, chapter 5.

text: Primum error est Orig. desumptus ex Platonis Timæo ; alterum probant fere Peripatetici, nec se Maximi rationibus putant admodum premi.
anchorLine: ἀποσφαλέντες, προϋπάρχειν Ἑλληνικῶς, ἢ μεθυπάρχειν Ἰουδαϊκῶς … ὑποτιθέμενοι ⁸⁸, ἀντιπαῦς πρὸς τοιούτων
en: The first is Origen's error, taken from Plato's Timaeus; the second the Peripatetics for the most part hold, nor do they think themselves much pressed by Maximus's arguments.
